Article Title: San Francisco techie shuts down video game that had players killing 'homeless people'; says: Made a personal donation to …
Article Text:
Developer says the game was built using AI tools

A San Francisco tech developer has apologized for creating a video game that turned the city’s notorious Tenderloin neighborhood into a zombie-killing zone. “Targeting people struggling with addiction or homelessness was never my intention” Pierre-Louis Biojout @plbiojout wrote in a post on X (formerly Twitter), further adding that he has taken down the game. The development comes after critics of the game argued that it allowed players to target homeless drug users. In addition to shutting down the game, the developer said that he has refunded all advertisers and also made a personal donation to a drug treatment and recovery service.“I built and posted a zombie game set on San Francisco streets. The setting and the way I promoted it showed poor judgment. Targeting people struggling with addiction or homelessness was never my intention,” the techie said.“I’ve taken the game and promotional posts down, refunded all advertisers, and made a personal donation to treatment and recovery services by Delancey Street equal to the game’s total revenue,” he further added.Pierre-Louis Biojout released a free, multiplayer browser game last week, describing it as a “Call of Duty style zombie shooter on the real SF streets.” The developer claimed that he built the game in just one weekend using the AI tools.He further revealed that he had taken $300 in advertising revenue.However, critics soon called out the game. “You think you’re being edgy but you’re just a huge piece of s–t,” one person wrote on social media. “Bring back shame. This is atrocious PR,” another fumed.City Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who represents the Tenderloin told the San Francisco Chronicle: “Turning violence against real people, including unhoused people, into entertainment is dehumanizing and should never be normalized”.
Article Summary: Pierre-Louis Biojout released a free, multiplayer browser game last week, describing it as a “Call of Duty style zombie shooter on the real SF streets” The developer claimed that he built the game in just one weekend using the AI tools. Critics soon called out the game.

Article Title: Elon Musk to Dario Amodei: I do not agree with your donation of Anthropic shares; I recommend …
Article Text:
Anthropic to allocate 5% of shares to public benefit fund

Anthropic has announced to donate a portion of the company’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), the Claude-maker said that it will start with giving away 5% of shares. “For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion,” the company, led by Dario Amodei said. “In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good. Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding,” the post continues. Elon Musk replied to Anthropic’s announcement recommending shares be distributed directly to the public instead of routed through an intermediary entity. “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public,” Musk wrote. “This is what I will be doing,” he said in another post.Here’s the full announcement made by Anthropic"Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows.Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as a wholly-owned LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad.Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones.In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report."
Article Summary: Anthropic to allocate 5% of shares to public benefit fund. Elon Musk replied to Anthropic’s announcement recommending shares be distributed directly to the public instead of routed through an intermediary entity. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue.

Article Title: Researchers equip giant cockroaches with medical backpacks, fitted with cameras and syringes, the cyborgs search trapped survivors to deliver life-saving aid in disasters
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

How these cyborg cockroaches work

What the tests reveal about the technology

How search and rescue teams could use them

Giant cockroaches could help rescue survivors after disasters. Researchers in Australia are developing cyborg-like insects equipped with miniature backpacks containing cameras, electronics and syringe systems designed to deliver emergency medication. The technology aims to help search-and-rescue teams locate injured people trapped beneath rubble and provide medical assistance when direct access is difficult.Called “paraborgs,” these modified insects combine their natural ability to navigate confined spaces with remotely controlled equipment. Scientists are testing whether the cockroaches can carry medical supplies into hazardous areas, identify potential victims through camera feeds and deliver drugs to targets. The approach could eventually support emergency responders dealing with collapsed buildings, earthquakes and other disasters where time and access are critical.According to a BGR report, the project involves researchers associated with the University of Queensland and the University of New South Wales. By combining insect movement with miniature electronic systems, the team aims to reach places conventional rescue equipment may struggle to access.The project uses the giant burrowing cockroach, scientifically known as Macropanesthia rhinoceros, a large cockroach species native to Australia. Its size makes it suitable for carrying a small electronic backpack containing a camera, control equipment and a syringe-based delivery mechanism.Unlike conventional robotic devices, these insects retain their natural ability to move through tight spaces. Researchers use implanted electrodes to stimulate the cockroaches' nervous systems, letting operators remotely control their direction. This could help guide them through gaps in collapsed structures and other areas human rescuers cannot easily enter.The cameras mounted on their backs provide a view of the surrounding environment. Rescue teams could use these images to assess obstacles, identify accessible routes and look for people who may be trapped nearby.The medical delivery system is another part of the design. Researchers have developed a mechanism that can fire a small syringe, described as functioning like a dart gun, towards a target. The aim is to deliver medication when a person needs urgent treatment and a medical professional cannot reach them immediately.Potential applications include delivering drugs to people experiencing certain emergencies, such as snakebite or severe allergic reactions. However, the technology remains experimental, and using it in real disaster rescue operations would require further testing.Early testing has examined whether the cockroaches can reach designated checkpoints and successfully deliver medication using the syringe mechanism.According to the reported results, the insects reached the checkpoints with a 100% success rate. The syringe system recorded a 72% success rate when delivering medication to targets. When the syringe was fired from within six inches of a target, the success rate increased to 95%.These results indicate that the insects can navigate designated routes under test conditions, while the distance between the syringe and its target remains an important factor in delivery accuracy.The findings also highlight the distinction between successfully guiding an insect to a location and delivering medicine accurately. In a real emergency, researchers would need to account for uneven terrain, limited visibility, unpredictable movement, and the injured person's condition.Further development would also be necessary to establish how the equipment performs in different environments and whether the system can deliver medication safely and consistently.Search and rescue operations often involve locating people in unstable buildings, collapsed structures and debris-filled areas. Sending rescuers into these environments can be difficult because of restricted access, falling material and the possibility of further structural collapse.Small insects equipped with cameras could provide another way to inspect such locations before a human rescuer enters. Their ability to move through narrow gaps could help teams gather information about spaces that are difficult to examine using larger equipment.Time is another consideration. Finding an injured person quickly can affect the treatment they receive, especially when the emergency involves a condition that requires prompt medical attention. Camera-equipped cockroaches could help rescuers assess a location and identify a possible route towards someone who needs assistance.The technology may also help reduce the physical demands placed on rescue workers. Rather than manually clearing every accessible section of debris, teams could first use the insects to inspect selected areas and determine where further intervention is needed.However, the system would not replace conventional rescue personnel or medical treatment. Its effectiveness would depend on camera visibility, remote control, access to the target, and the ability to safely deliver the appropriate medication.For now, the research demonstrates a potential application of biohybrid technology, which combines living organisms with electronic systems. If further testing establishes its reliability and safety, these cyborg cockroaches could become an additional tool for locating and assisting disaster survivors in places where conventional rescue equipment has limited access.
Article Summary: Researchers in Australia are developing cyborg-like insects equipped with miniature backpacks containing cameras, electronics and syringe systems. The technology aims to help search-and-rescue teams locate injured people trapped beneath rubble and provide medical assistance when direct access is difficult. Scientists are testing whether the cockroaches can carry medical supplies into hazardous areas.

Article Title: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang praises Mark Zuckerberg, he replies: I have never gotten such a nice…
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang

‘ Very Bayesian ’: Rapid decisive conviction

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and company CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision-making. During a recent interview, Meta’s Wang was asked about the qualities of Facebook founder, and he offered glowing praise for Zuckerberg, highlighting his exceptional willingness to make massive, rapid pivots based on core convictions. During the conversation Wang was specifically asked how Zuckerberg differed as a leader from what he initially anticipated. Before Wang could reply, Zuckerberg opened with a lighthearted quip, joking, “I think I can leave now.” Wang quickly followed up with his perspective on their working relationship over the past year.Wang noted that while he does not have an extensive set of comparisons, observing Zuckerberg's management style firsthand revealed unique traits that stand out even within elite tech founder circles:“One of the very cool things about working with Mark over the past year has just been watching the true degree of his boldness,” Wang explained, adding, “Once he internalises certain beliefs, like the speed and magnitude of willing to change prior actions and pivot towards the worldview that is consistent with those beliefs, I think these are pretty unusual traits, generally speaking, even among this base of founders. Very Bayesian.”The analytical praise drew a warm, humorous reaction from Zuckerberg.“Very Bayesian. I've never gotten such a nice compliment,” Zuckerberg responded.A person who follows the Bayesian method relies on statistical inference, using Bayes' theorem to update the probability of a hypothesis as new data or evidence becomes available.Expanding on his observations, Wang admitted that Zuckerberg's appetite for sweeping strategic gambles initially took him by surprise before earning his deep respect.“No, but then I think also just the degree of boldness. It was actually quite puzzling to me at first, the degree to which you were willing to make these massive bets. That is quite a notable trait and something I really admire,” Wang continued.Zuckerberg concluded the exchange with appreciation for the assessment, replying: “I'm so flattered.”
Article Summary: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision- making. Wang noted that observing Zuckerberg's management style firsthand revealed unique traits that stand out even within elite tech founder circles.

Article Title: Boat expands global footprint with Sri Lanka, Bhutan launch; international revenue surges in FY26
Article Text: Homegrown audio and wearables brand Boat has expanded its international presence with its entry into Sri Lanka and Bhutan, as the company looks to accelerate growth beyond India under its "Boat 2.0" strategy. The company said its international revenue more than doubled in FY26, a performance it described as an early validation of its efforts to build markets outside India. The latest expansion strengthens Boat's footprint across South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region.Boat will launch a multi-category portfolio in both Sri Lanka and Bhutan, covering personal audio products, smartwatches and charging solutions. The company said it plans to tailor its offerings over time based on local consumer preferences and market demand.The move comes as Boat seeks to diversify its growth drivers after establishing itself as a leading player in India's audio and wearables market. International markets are expected to play a key role in the company's next phase of growth, alongside expansion into newer consumer technology categories.According to Boat, Sri Lanka and Bhutan offer attractive opportunities due to their young, increasingly digital-first populations, rising adoption of personal electronics and familiarity with Indian brands and popular culture. Commenting on the expansion, Gaurav Nayyar, CEO of Boat, said the company's international strategy is focused on building relevance market by market rather than simply expanding product availability."For us, international expansion is not about putting the same products on more shelves. It is about building market by market, understanding local consumers and creating relevance in each geography," Nayyar said.He added that the company aims to build Boat into a global lifestyle technology brand originating from India, competing on product design, innovation and consumer understanding.The international push comes amid a broader evolution of Boat's business. While audio remains its core category, the company said it has expanded its capabilities in wearables, charging solutions and other emerging technology segments. It added that its wearables business turned profitable in FY26, while charging solutions and other emerging categories contributed a growing share of profits.Supporting the expansion is Boat Labs, the company's in-house research and development centre, which employs more than 100 engineers focused on product development and innovation across categories.Going forward, Boat said it plans to deepen its presence in existing overseas markets while evaluating further expansion opportunities across South Asia, Southeast Asia, the GCC and other high-potential regions.
Article Summary: Boat will launch a multi-category portfolio in both Sri Lanka and Bhutan. The company said it plans to tailor its offerings over time based on local consumer preferences and market demand. The move comes as Boat seeks to diversify its growth drivers after establishing itself as a leading player in India's audio and wearables market.

Article Title: URBN Bloq Magtag 10,000mAh Qi2 magnetic wireless power bank launched at Rs 2,499
Article Text:
URBN Bloq Magtag : Price and availability

URBN Bloq Magtag: Key highlights

URBN has launched the Bloq Magtag power bank. The new magnetic wireless power bank is designed for users who want a portable charging solution for everyday use and travel. The accessory combines magnetic wireless charging with wired fast charging, letting users power compatible smartphones wirelessly or charge devices via USB-C.It features a soft-matte finish and a compact design that makes it easier to carry while commuting, travelling, or working away from a power outlet. The power bank also supports charging two devices and includes safety features under the company's URBN SAFE programme. It comes in three colours and supports Qi2 wireless charging, adding another charging option for compatible devices.The URBN Bloq Magtag magnetic wireless power bank has been launched in India at Rs 2,499. It comes in White, Black, and Blue. You can buy it online and offline, including Croma, Reliance Digital, Vijay Sales, Amazon, Flipkart, Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, and URBN's official website, UrbnWorld.com.The URBN Bloq Magtag comes with a 10,000mAh battery and supports 15W Qi2 magnetic wireless charging and 20W wired charging speeds. The company claims that the product uses magnetic alignment to keep a secure wireless connection with compatible devices while charging.For users who prefer wired charging, the power bank supports 20W USB-C fast charging. It also supports dual-device charging, letting users charge two devices wirelessly and wired.The power bank features a soft-matte finish and a compact, portable form factor. URBN says its magnetic alignment system helps position compatible devices for wireless charging.The URBN Bloq Magtag has a flight-safe design and, according to the company, can be carried in hand luggage during air travel. Its compact size makes it ideal for frequent travellers or those who spend extended periods away from a power outlet.The power bank also comes with URBN SAFE, the company's safety programme that includes multiple safety checks and circuit-level safeguards. These measures support safe, reliable charging.
Article Summary: URBN has launched the Bloq Magtag power bank in India at Rs 2,499. The accessory combines magnetic wireless charging with wired fast charging. It comes in three colours and supports Qi2 wireless charging, adding another charging option for compatible devices.

Article Title: Meta’s ‘highest-paid employee’ Alexandr Wang on the WhatsApp message from Mark Zuckerberg that changed his career: Have time for a...
Article Text:
Meta AI chief Alexander Wang with CEO Mark Zuckerberg

Alexandr Wang's memo told Zuckerberg to hire fewer, better people

Meta's CFO warned Wang the AI bet had to work

Muse and Muse Wonder have put Meta back in the AI race

In April 2025, Alexandr Wang was sitting in a staff meeting at Scale AI, the data-labelling company he co-founded, when his phone pinged. It was a WhatsApp message from Mark Zuckerberg : "Have time for a call?" Wang's first thought, as he tells it now, was simply, "huh, interesting."That call ran for 44 minutes. Within two months, Meta had put $14.3 billion into Scale AI for a 49% stake and brought Wang in to run its AI efforts. Wang and Zuckerberg retold the story together on Cheeky Pint, the podcast hosted by Stripe co-founder John Collison, in an episode recorded around the release of Meta's new Muse Wonder AI model.The timing of that message matters. Meta had released its Llama 4 models on April 4, 2025, to a lukewarm response. Around April 20, Zuckerberg said, he started calling people across the industry for advice on what to do next. Wang was one of them.Two days after the call, Wang sent Zuckerberg a long memo. Zuckerberg described it on Cheeky Pint as Wang laying out what he would do "if I were in your position."The first point was about people, and how few of them Meta needed. "The very first thing is that you don't need a lot of people, and talent density is the thing that matters," Zuckerberg recalled.That idea still shapes Meta Superintelligence Labs. Its core research team numbers under 200, "closer to 100," according to Wang, inside a company of roughly 75,000 employees.The hire raised eyebrows. Wang, now 29, is an MIT dropout who built Scale AI into a key data supplier for the big AI labs, but he had never trained a frontier model. Collison pointed this out on the show. Zuckerberg said he spoke to the heads of research at all the major labs before deciding, and came away sure: "Alex is the guy."What followed was a recruiting sprint Zuckerberg called "supernova." He cleared his calendar for a month or two just to meet researchers. "I don't think either of us slept that much for the first couple of months," he said.Wang also recalled one early meeting that left him uneasy. When he said Meta's first priority should be a strong reasoning model, one of the existing leads asked whether consumers needed one at all. Wang said he called Nat Friedman, now head of Meta's AI products, straight after.By the end of 2025, the numbers had become enormous. Zuckerberg said Meta was preparing to "write this check for like, I don't know, like $100 billion, $200 billion" before anyone had seen the new models. "I'm like, Alex, are you sure this is going to work?"At an executive gathering in Hawaii, Wang said, CFO Susan Li pulled him aside several times to drive the point home. "If it's good, it's all good. We're great. But if it's bad, it's really, really, really bad." Wang admitted that all he had to show at the time was a "vibe report" on research progress and a few plots.The bet produced Muse Spark in April 2026, followed by the Muse personal agent app on September 8. Muse climbed to the top of Apple's App Store within days. Wang's own Muse, which he named Oiler, buys increasingly obscure teas from farms in Taiwan and Japan every week. Zuckerberg uses his to critique his MMA technique in the one-minute breaks between rounds.On October 12, Meta released Muse Wonder, the first model it calls frontier-class. For now, it sits behind paid Muse subscriptions. Zuckerberg said the team was "very, very critical" of its own work along the way, and Wang describes the lab as a room full of "insecure overachievers."Asked what kind of boss Zuckerberg is, Wang called him "very Bayesian," someone who updates his beliefs and then moves the whole company to match. A five-word WhatsApp message, and the 44-minute call that followed, is about as clear an example of that as Meta has.
Article Summary: Alexandr Wang was brought in by Mark Zuckerberg to run Meta's AI efforts. Wang and Zuckerberg retold the story on Cheeky Pint, the podcast hosted by Stripe co- founder John Collison. The bet produced Muse Spark in April 2026, followed by the Muse personal agent app.

Article Title: As investors debate if Accenture will be a winner or loser from AI, the company may be planning to say 'goodbye' to China, after receiving unsolicited ...
Article Text:
As investors debate if Accenture will be a winner or loser from AI, the company may be planning to say 'goodbye' to China, after receiving unsolicited ...

Accenture stock has seen ups and down this year

How billions from 'China office' sale may help

Accenture is reportedly exploring a potential $1.5 billion sale of its operations in China. According to a report in Financial Times, 'Chinese operations' sale talks come as the world’s largest publicly traded IT consultancy Accenture sharpens its focus on faster-growing markets and seeks to reassure investors over its strategy in the artificial intelligence era.The Dublin-headquartered company has enlisted JPMorgan to conduct a strategic review of the unit following unsolicited approaches over the past year, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times. The entire Greater China division, which encompasses mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, could command a valuation of up to $1.5 billion.People close to the discussions noted that any formal process is anticipated to attract interest from private equity companies alongside a select group of strategic suitors. Accenture may choose to maintain a meaningful minority holding to preserve continuity for existing multinational and domestic clients, though discussions remain preliminary and may not result in a final transaction.The strategic deliberations coincide with broader volatility for Accenture's stock, as markets evaluate whether consultancy giants will benefit from companies adoption artificial intelligence or suffer as clients automate internal workflows previously handled by external contractors.Meanwhile, tightening data security and cross-border regulatory scrutiny in Beijing has prompted several Western advisory firms, including McKinsey, to scale back their Chinese footprints, segregate technology infrastructure, and navigate hurdles to international integration.The potential divestment would provide fresh capital as Accenture positions itself for long-term artificial intelligence deployment. Speaking at a recent investor gathering, chief financial officer Angie Park noted that the firm retains an established history of exiting businesses, offerings, and regional operations that fall short of strategic or return targets. Management reiterated plans to deploy efficiency gains into customer pricing and targeted acquisitions, while upholding shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases.The move follows long-range guidance outlined by the consultancy, in which it projected subdued top-line expansion across the next two years ahead of an expected acceleration toward the end of the decade driven by enterprise AI adoption. Wall Street responded favorably to the outlook and recent earnings outperformance, with analysts pointing to expanding opportunities across its $3tn addressable market as the consultancy recalibrates its global footprint.
Article Summary: Accenture is reportedly exploring a potential $1.5 billion sale of its operations in China. The sale would provide fresh capital as Accenture positions itself for long-term artificial intelligence deployment. The entire Greater China division, which encompasses mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, could command a valuation of up to $2 billion.

Article Title: In 2025, Japan warned Microsoft of a 'message scam', software giant traced it to China months later, blocking three online stores that hit 75,000 companies across the globe
Article Text:
What Japan ‘alerted’ Microsoft about

In a major coordinated offensive against transnational cybercrime, Microsoft and the Health Information Sharing and Analysis Center have seized and redirected the online infrastructure powering three Chinese-language cybercrime stores known as YAM Store, CoGUI and Iron Man. Acting under an order granted by the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida, investigators dismantled an illicit ecosystem that has fueled over one billion malicious messages across more than 150 countries since January. The sweeping attacks targeted consumers, banks, healthcare networks, and over 75,000 organizations globally, generating tens of millions of dollars for their operators while directing more than 750 million fraudulent messages at Microsoft customers alone.Steven Masada, general manager of Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit, warned that seemingly routine scam messages are frequently just the visible tip of expansive transnational syndicates. Masada noted that while YAM Store, CoGUI and Iron Man represent only a segment of a broader criminal network, severing their infrastructure severely hampers scammers' ability to acquire the compromised accounts and automated toolsets necessary to stage high-volume attacks.The international takedown originated from an inquiry in late 2025, when Japan’s National Police Agency alerted Microsoft to localized phishing surges hitting Japanese residents. The probe quickly broadened into a global coalition involving the Japan Cybercrime Control Center, security and technology firms including Cloudflare, Oracle, Proofpoint, Resecurity, and TRM Labs, alongside intelligence sharing with the U.S. Secret Service and international law enforcement bodies.According to Microsoft Threat Intelligence, the illicit operations functioned as commercial, turnkey fraud clearinghouses developed by Chinese-speaking threat actors. YAM Store mirrored an everyday e-commerce storefront, allowing prospective scammers to compare prices and buy ready-made exploitation kits alongside illicit Microsoft and Google accounts. The syndicate frequently bought expired domains previously owned by schools and charities, reviving the sites to generate Microsoft 365 tenant accounts before accepting payment via Alipay, WeChat Pay, and Tether cryptocurrency.Meanwhile, CoGUI and its mid-year successor, Iron Man, equipped threat actors with off-the-shelf phishing sites and deceptive templates mimicking credible entities. Investigators cataloged more than 2,300 Iron Man lure variations impersonating financial institutions, healthcare providers, police departments, and state agencies, with US-focused schemes heavily skewing toward transit notices, unpaid parking citations, and traffic fines. The end goal centered on siphoning credentials and financial card data to execute unauthorized payments and purchase luxury merchandise.Following the federal court order, Microsoft disabled over 20,000 accounts directly tied to YAM Store and instituted active blocks against more than 100,000 malicious domains used for brand impersonation and wire fraud, blunting the operational reach of the syndicate.
Article Summary: Microsoft seized and redirected the online infrastructure powering three Chinese-language cybercrime stores. Investigators dismantled an illicit ecosystem that has fueled over one billion malicious messages across more than 150 countries since January. The sweeping attacks targeted consumers, banks, healthcare networks, and over 75,000 organizations globally.

Article Title: Michael Dell is the biggest donor to Trump Accounts, but his home state came first for his charity; in April he gave $750 million to…
Article Text:
The Dells’ $250 deposits go to kids who miss the federal $1,000 seed

Texas has been at the centre of Dell philanthropy for over two decades

UT Austin’s AI-native medical centre will carry the Dell name

Michael Dell and his wife, Susan Dell, are now the single largest private backers of Trump Accounts, the new US government investment accounts for children. Their $6.25 billion pledge puts $250 into the accounts of 25 million American kids aged 10 and under, and the couple said earlier this month that the full amount would be deposited within days.It is the biggest gift the Dells have ever made, more than double what their foundation gave away in its first 26 years. Most of their giving before this stayed in Texas, where Michael Dell started his company from a University of Texas at Austin (UT Austin) dorm room in 1984. In April, the couple became the first donors to cross $1 billion in lifetime giving to the university, with a $750 million commitment for a new medical campus.Trump Accounts were created under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and opened on July 4. The Treasury seeds $1,000 into the accounts of children born between 2025 and 2028. The Dells’ money covers older children who don’t qualify, provided they live in ZIP codes where the median family income is $150,000 or less. Families can add up to $5,000 a year, and the money unlocks when the child turns 18.By October 7, more than 10 million children had received the Dell deposit, worth $2.6 billion.That was the same as the total philanthropic money the White House said had gone into the accounts at that point.Michael Dell has also backed a new rule letting donors put individual company shares into the accounts, after SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell pledged over 2 million shares to children aged 11 to 17. Critics say this ties a child’s savings to one company. Dell said in an interview that he found it hard to see one share of SpaceX as a bad thing.The ties have drawn scrutiny. President Donald Trump has repeatedly urged Americans to buy Dell computers, and in May the company’s federal unit won a $9.7 billion Pentagon contract that some government oversight experts questioned. The White House says Trump’s praise is about the donation alone.The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation, set up in 1999, runs over 800 projects a year across the US, Africa, India and Israel, but its biggest bets have been in Central Texas. Dell Children’s Medical Center opened in Austin in 2007, and in 2013 the couple put $50 million into founding Dell Medical School at UT Austin. After Hurricane Harvey, they committed over $43 million to rebuilding across 41 counties.Susan Dell, who chairs the foundation, drives much of this. Her father was a surgical oncologist, and health has been her cause since childhood. As a girl, she would stop strangers at the grocery store to tell them not to smoke.The April money funds the UT Dell Campus for Advanced Research, centred on a UT Dell Medical Center due in 2030 and designed around AI and advanced computing from the start. MD Anderson Cancer Center will run cancer care inside it, and the gift also covers supercomputing, scholarships and student housing.It ranks among the largest gifts any American university has received. UT Austin has used it to set two targets: raise $10 billion in 10 years and break into the country’s top 10 medical centres within a decade.Even the Trump Accounts gift began as a Texas plan. Michael Dell has said the couple first thought about keeping it to their home state before deciding to take it nationwide.
Article Summary: $6.25 billion pledge puts $250 into the accounts of 25 million kids aged 10 and under. It is the biggest gift the Dells have ever made, more than double what their foundation gave away in its first 26 years. Most of their giving before this stayed in Texas, where Michael Dell started his company from a University of Texas at Austin dorm room in 1984.

Article Title: Google Pixel 11’s exclusive anti-endless scrolling feature is coming to older Pixel phones: What is it and how it works
Article Text:
What is ‘Pause Point’ and how does it work

Moving beyond the Pixel 11 exclusivity

A standout Digital Wellbeing feature designed to curb endless app scrolling is no longer locked exclusively to the Google Pixel 11. Known as Pause Point, the feature originally debuted as a signature capability for Google 's newest flagship lineup, but it is now expanding to older Pixel smartphones via the Android 17 QPR1 update – and is already beginning to appear on third-party devices such as OnePlus, a report has said. According to Android Authority, the expansion brings fresh relief to users struggling with screen time and looking for automatic interventions to break the cycle of continuous, compulsive scrolling.First announced by Google in May ahead of its annual I/O developer conference, Pause Point is an addition to Google’s built-in Digital Wellbeing suite. The feature operates as an active speed bump against ‘doomscrolling’.Instead of merely tracking how many hours you spend inside an app, Pause Point introduces a short mindfulness break directly on your screen, asking users to set a duration for which they want to use the app. When you get lost in an endless feed or an obsessive app session, the tool steps in to pause the interface, prompting you to disengage, reflect and put the device down.While smartphones offer immense utility, their ability to monopolise attention has made digital downtime harder to protect.Pause Point is built specifically to intercept those subconscious impulses before screen time spirals out of hand.Following its initial reveal in May, reports suggested that Google planned to treat Pause Point as an exclusive selling point reserved solely for the Pixel 11 series. However, Google shifted course with the rollout of Android 17 QPR1, deploying the functionality to older generations of Pixel hardware.Now, the feature is spreading beyond Google's own hardware footprint. Pause Point has been confirmed running on a OnePlus 13R running the ColorOS 17 beta, marking its first documented appearance on an Android device running an external manufacturer skin.While Google’s official support documentation still states that Pause Point “is available on Pixel 11 series running Android 17 and later,” its successful operation on ColorOS indicates that the capability is preparing for a broader, general rollout across Android 17 handsets equipped with Google's Digital Wellbeing package.
Article Summary: Pause Point was first announced by Google in May ahead of its annual I/O developer conference. The feature operates as an active speed bump against ‘doomscrolling’ Instead of merely tracking how many hours you spend inside an app, Pause Point introduces a short mindfulness break directly on your screen.

Article Title: Roblox bets big on India: Company India MD Sunil Rao says ‘next big hit on Roblox could come from this country’
Article Text:
Sunil Rao, Managing Director Roblox India and South Asia

What Roblox offers creators in India

Roblox India: What the numbers say

India has more than 500 million gamers, the world’s second-largest gaming population. The report expects video game revenues to rise from Rs 6,300 crore in 2025 to Rs 9,200 crore by 2028. That is 13% annual growth, against 5.1% globally.

Daily active users in India grew at a compound annual rate of 76% between 2020 and 2025, reaching millions of users.

The number of Indian creators eligible for Roblox payouts grew at a compound annual rate of 96% over the same period, passing 250 in 2025. Total payouts grew 72% a year. Among surveyed creators who publish on several platforms, Roblox made up 61% of their creation revenue.

About 91% of surveyed creators say their Roblox work helped them get job offers, freelance projects or business opportunities.

Among surveyed Indian users, 88% play on mobile phones, 92% like learning at their own pace with free tutorials, 93% enjoy spending time with friends on the platform and 94% say it helps them unwind.

Access Partnership estimates that creator activity added Rs 123.9 crore to India’s GDP between 2020 and 2025. It also supported about 510 full-time-equivalent jobs in 2025.

Roblox also released an Economic Impact report for India, which it says shows its interest in investing in the country’s creator ecosystem. Sunil Rao, managing director of Roblox India and South Asia, highlighted the platform’s potential in the country, saying that “the next big hit could come from India.”“This is the age of small studios and the next big hit on Roblox could come from India. Roblox daily active users grew by 64% y-o-y* and I am excited about the possibilities that exist in this market across players, partners and creators,” he added. Roblox believes the platform can play a key role in growing both game consumption and creator careers in India. (*The growth figure is for the quarter ending June 30, 2026.)Rao announced that Roblox will launch Build in India soon. It was first announced at RDC 2026. Additionally, Roblox launched in Hindi a few months ago, and more languages are coming soon. Moreover, creators can earn from their experiences through monetisation inside the app. Roblox Studio, a free to use service, helps people build experiences and also teaches design skills.Roblox report highlights several figures about the company and India:

Article Title: Google cofounder Sergey Brin has donated $100 million, more than any billionaire, opposing California's Wealth Tax, but he cannot cast a vote next month as ...
Article Text:
Sergey Brin’s move to Nevada linked to tax concerns

What is California's Proposition 40

Billionaires and Gavin Newsom line up against it

Larry Page also shifts residency

Google cofounder Sergey Brin has emerged as the biggest financial opponent of California’s proposed billionaire wealth tax, contributing more than $100 million to campaigns against the measure. However, the tech billionaire will not be eligible to vote on the proposal next month after changing his voter registration from California to Nevada, according to a Forbes report. Brin has channelled his opposition to the tax through his Build a Better California PAC, making him the largest donor fighting the initiative. The irony, Forbes noted, is that Brin himself will not get a say at the ballot box because public records from the Nevada Secretary of State's office show he changed his voter registration to Nevada on December 10.According to Forbes, Brin's relocation appears to be part of a broader effort to avoid the proposed tax, which would apply only to California residents as of January 1, 2026.The billionaire purchased a $42 million mansion on the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe in December, and his representatives told Forbes that he is now a Nevada resident.The move also makes Brin, whose net worth is estimated at $263 billion, the richest resident of Nevada, surpassing casino heiress and Republican donor Miriam Adelson, whose fortune is estimated at $31.2 billion.Brin's voter registration reportedly lists his political affiliation as nonpartisan.Proposition 40 will be on the ballot in November. It would impose a one-time 5% tax on California’s 200 billionaires. Ninety percent of the revenue would go to the state’s health care program. The remaining 10% would go to education, food assistance and administration. With a net worth of nearly $260 billion, Brin could owe about $13 billion if it passes.Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel have also donated to groups opposing the measure. Brin has likened the proposal to the socialist society he left behind. “I fled socialism with my family in 1979,” he told The New York Times in April, adding that he does not want California to end up in the same place.Gov. Gavin Newsom has also come out against the tax. He argues it would erode the state’s tax base and cut revenue for social services. In an interview with Bloomberg Businessweek earlier this year, he said it would reduce investment in education, teachers, librarians, childcare, firefighting and police.Forbes reported that Brin's Google cofounder Larry Page has likewise moved away from California, although he is not yet registered to vote in Florida, according to records reviewed by the publication.Page's representatives told Forbes that his residency has changed from California to Florida. The billionaire reportedly spent $173 million on two Miami mansions between December 2025 and January 2026. With an estimated net worth of $286 billion, Page is now said to be the second-richest resident of Florida, behind Jeff Bezos, whose fortune is estimated at $374 billion.Representatives for both Brin and Page did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding their voter registration status, Forbes said.
Article Summary: Google cofounder Sergey Brin changed his voter registration from California to Nevada on December 10. His net worth is estimated at $263 billion, making him the richest resident of Nevada. Brin has channelled his opposition to the tax through his Build a Better California PAC. His Google cofounder Larry Page has likewise moved away from California, although he is not yet registered to vote in Florida.

Article Title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang reveals the man who made the 'impossible' possible between Apple and Meta
Article Text:
Tim Cook-Mark Zuckerberg once clashed over privacy

Meta's most capable open AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio

Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang has revealed that former Apple executive Daniel Gross played a key role in bringing the iPhone-maker and Meta together for an AI collaboration. After years of disagreements, the two companies are now working together to run Meta's new Muse Spark Open AI model on Apple's high-end Mac Studio computers. Their collaboration allows Muse Spark Open, which has 816 billion parameters, to run across two or four connected Mac Studios powered by Apple's M5 Ultra chips, using Apple's MLX framework. Alexandr Wang told Axios that Gross, who now works at Meta, helped the two sides work together. Wang revealed that the two companies had been working together for several months.“I think he played a really big role in kind of getting the two companies to work nicely together,” Alexandr Wang told the publication. “We're excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again,” he said.The rivalry between Apple and Meta (then Facebook) dates back to 2018 during the Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal. The then Apple CEO Tim Cook was asked what he would do if he were Mark Zuckerberg. Tim Cook then replied saying “I wouldn't be in this situation”.Later, Mark Zuckerberg called Cook's comments "extremely glib.” Again in 2021, when Apple introduced new privacy protections, Zuckerberg told employees that Facebook needed to "inflict pain" on Apple over the dispute, per a report by the Wall Street Journal then.Muse Spark Open is an 816-billion-parameter model built on a mixture-of-experts design. Meta calls it the most capable US-developed open-weight model to date. It is aimed at long coding sessions, multi-step reasoning and video analysis. The model is free to download from platforms like Hugging Face, and its licence allows commercial use with some limits.The setup links two or four Mac Studios running Apple's M5 Ultra chip. Apple's MLX framework splits the model across those machines. Apple has also put out new benchmarks and technical notes on how MLX handles open models of this size. Since everything stays on the desk, Meta does not see the prompts or files developers feed it. "Meta has no control or visibility to any of that," Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said.It does not come cheap. An M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 256GB of memory costs over Rs 9 lakh at US prices, and the model needs at least two. A 512GB version is due later this month.
Article Summary: Meta's Muse Spark Open AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio computers. Former Apple executive Daniel Gross played a key role in bringing the two companies together for an AI collaboration. The rivalry between Apple and Meta dates back to 2018 during the Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal.

Article Title: What is CXMT's 'Chinese chip bomb' that has wiped billions off the US stock market
Article Text:
One Chinese chip design, billions gone from Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung (Picture: Reuters)

CXMT's 4F² chip design squeezes more memory into less space

Why Micron and SK Hynix have so much to lose right now

CXMT still has no answer to HBM, the memory inside AI chips

A Chinese memory chipmaker that few investors outside China had heard of until this summer has spent the past week knocking billions of dollars off the world's biggest chip stocks. ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, says it has made "key progress" on a denser memory chip design, and the news has sent Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung and a string of storage companies sharply lower.The worry is specific. CXMT plans to bring a server memory module built on the new design to market by the end of 2026, aiming straight at the part of the memory business where AI demand has pushed prices and profits to record highs. SK Hynix fell more than 10% in Seoul on Tuesday, Samsung dropped 7.4% and South Korea's Kospi lost 5.5%. In the US, the Philadelphia semiconductor index slid for a fifth straight session, with Micron, Seagate and Western Digital among the hardest hit.CXMT president Cao Kanyu outlined the plan at an industry event in Shanghai on October 10. The technology is called 4F², also written as 4F square, where F is the smallest feature a chipmaker can print on silicon.Mainstream DRAM cells today take up about 6F². Cutting that to 4F² shrinks each cell by roughly a third, which in theory fits 50% more cells into the same area.The first product will be a DDR5 RDIMM, the memory module that sits inside data centre servers. CXMT credits a vertical transistor design that keeps electrical leakage in check as cells get smaller.Samsung and SK Hynix are chasing the same architecture, and SK Hynix published a roadmap for it last year. A Chinese rival widely seen as a step behind claiming progress first is what rattled the market.Memory has been the most profitable corner of the AI boom this year. Micron's revenue for the quarter ended September jumped to $54.23 billion from $11.32 billion a year earlier, and its gross margin climbed to 86.8%. Those numbers rest on a shortage, so even the prospect of a new supplier puts that pricing power in question.CXMT is no small player either. HSBC estimates its share of the global DRAM market has grown to about 10%, from roughly 4% a year ago. The Hefei-based company raised $8.6 billion in Asia's biggest IPO of the year in July. On Friday, it reported preliminary nine-month profit of up to 132.5 billion yuan (about $19.8 billion), against a loss of 5.3 billion yuan a year earlier.Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth, called it profit-taking, noting that when competition looms, "all the sheep run to the door at the same time." Broadcom CEO Hock Tan comparing AI spending to gambling a day earlier did little for the mood.Several analysts think the selloff ran ahead of reality. CXMT has not shown it can make the new chips in volume, and server customers take months to approve a new supplier. The plan also leaves out high-bandwidth memory, or HBM, the stacked memory that sits next to Nvidia's AI processors, where SK Hynix and Samsung remain far ahead. US export controls keep the most advanced chipmaking machines out of China too.Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra still expects demand to outrun supply through 2027 and 2028, with more than three-quarters of next year's output already spoken for.The chip index is up over 70% this year, which leaves plenty of room for nervous selling. Whether CXMT's design becomes a real threat will be clear once its first server modules reach customers around the end of the year.
Article Summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, says it has made "key progress" on a denser memory chip design. The news has sent Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung and a string of storage companies sharply lower. CX MT plans to bring a server memory module built on the new design to market by 2026.

Article Title: Canadian billionaire Kevin O Leary: Till few years ago, I always told everyone that the only education you should get is Engineering, Engineering, and Engineering; but no longer as now the highest-pai

Kevin O’Leary: I don’t believe in only engineering anymore

Kevin’O Leary believes creators changing how businesses find customers

What 'O Leary means

'Amazing what's happening to the arts'

Read Kevin O’Leary’s post here

I used to say just a few years ago, the only education you should get is engineering, engineering, and engineering. I don't believe that anymore because storytelling, photography, video editing, and creators, are changing the landscape for both large and small businesses by acquiring customers. It's not a $48,000 career anymore, it's more like a $400,000 career because they’re doing the contracts with multiple companies, showing them how to reduce their customer acquisition cost and increase their return on ad spend.

That's the opportunity. It's amazing what's happening to the arts.

Canadian billionaire and Shark Tank Judge Kevin O’Leary has said he no longer believes engineering is the only educational path that guarantees career success, arguing that storytelling and digital content creation have emerged among the most lucrative skills in today's economy. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), O'Leary said his views on education and high-demand careers have shifted significantly over the past few years as businesses increasingly rely on creators and digital marketers to acquire customers and grow revenue."I used to say just a few years ago, the only education you should get is engineering, engineering, and engineering. I don't believe that anymore," O'Leary wrote. According to O'Leary, skills such as storytelling, photography and video editing are reshaping the way both large and small companies attract customers. He said creators are becoming essential business partners because they help brands lower customer acquisition costs and improve returns on advertising spending.O’Leary said storytelling, photography, video editing and content creation are reshaping the landscape for both large and small businesses by helping them acquire customers.“It’s not a $48,000 career anymore, it’s more like a $400,000 career because they’re doing the contracts with multiple companies,” he said. He added that creators are showing companies how to reduce their customer acquisition cost and increase their return on ad spend. “That’s the opportunity,” he said. He ended with a nod to the creative fields: “It’s amazing what’s happening to the arts.”Customer acquisition cost is how much a business spends to win one new customer. Return on ad spend measures the revenue earned for every dollar spent on advertising. O’Leary’s argument is that creators who can produce content that brings in customers cheaply are being paid by several companies at once, rather than working for a single employer on a fixed salary. The $48,000 and $400,000 figures are O’Leary’s own and were not accompanied by a source. He did not say what group of workers they refer to or whether the higher number represents typical or top-end earnings.O'Leary said the growing demand for content creators highlights a broader shift in the economy, where creative professionals are increasingly driving business growth."That's the opportunity. It's amazing what's happening to the arts," he said.
Article Summary: Kevin O'Leary says storytelling, photography, video editing and content creation are reshaping the landscape for both large and small businesses by helping them acquire customers. He said creators are becoming essential business partners because they help brands lower customer acquisition costs and improve returns on advertising spending.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai, 'Godfather of AI' Yann LeCun reply to Elon Musk post that says ‘future has flying cars’
Article Text:
Tesla roadster demo

Yann LeCun breaks down the physics: ‘Just compressed air’

Even assuming that 50% of the mass of the car is the compressed air, that gives you less than 10s of useful thrust (with thrust-to-weight ratio larger than 1.0).

Probably more like 5 seconds, actually.

So the car must be an empty, lightweight shell containing big compressed air tanks.

Cute demo, but totally impractical.

But of course, you knew that.

Compressed air vs. rocket propulsion

Hydrogen peroxide rockets (like the individual jetpacks of the 1970s) have a specific impulse of 150s, about 3x compressed air, without the annoying exponentially decreasing maximum thrust of compressed air jets.

I originally guessed the car might have used hydrogen peroxide jets because of all the steam. But that's just condensation caused rapid depressurization

Elon Musk set social media abuzz after sharing dramatic footage of a thruster-equipped Tesla Roadster lifting off the ground, somersaulting mid-air and then landing perfectly on ground. The Tesla CEO declared that the “future does have flying cars”. The post triggered massive online engagement, drawing playful reactions from tech peers, including Google CEO Sundar Pichai. However, it also drew technical skepticism from former Meta Chief AI Scientist Yann LeCun, who labeled the stunt a “cute demo, but totally impractical.”As per the video, as the vehicle lifts off, it spews thick plumes of smoke, ‘flies’ over stationary Tesla vehicles, including a Tesla Semi and tumbles as dense vapor blankets the surrounding tarmac. Pichai quipped: “The FSD version of this will be something:) congrats!”Musk responded warmly to the exchange, writing: “Thanks ❤️🚀 It’s such an honor working with incredible engineers.”While the demonstration delighted fans, LeCun took to social media to analyse the underlying mechanics, questioning the vehicle’s real-world feasibility. Initially wondering whether the system ran on hydrogen peroxide rocket propellant, LeCun concluded the thrusters were simply powered by cold gas: “Okay, so it's just compressed air. Easier. But crappy specific impulse (less than 50 seconds).”LeCun argued that the physics behind compressed gas severely restrict flight duration and payload capacity:Drawing comparisons to older aerospace experiments, LeCun pointed out that 1970s-era individual jetpacks relied on hydrogen peroxide rockets, which deliver a specific impulse of roughly 150 seconds.
Article Summary: Elon Musk posted video of himself flying a Tesla Roadster in the air. The stunt drew the attention of tech peers, including Google CEO Sundar Pichai. But it also drew technical skepticism from former Meta Chief AI Scientist Yann LeCun, who labelled the stunt a ‘cute demo, but totally impractical’
