Article Title: Rs 3 lakh iPhone Duo sells out within minutes of preorders on Apple Store, deliveries slip to January 2027
Article Text:
Every iPhone Duo model now ships in late January

Tight supply is behind the long iPhone Duo wait

Apple's first foldable iPhone sold out within minutes of preorders opening on Friday, and anyone placing an order now will have to wait until the new year to get one. Preorders for the iPhone Duo went live at 5:30pm IST on October 16, and delivery estimates slipped from next week to late January almost as soon as the order pages loaded.The picture in India is no different. A 256GB Star White iPhone Duo, which carries an MRP of Rs 2,99,900, currently shows a delivery date of Saturday, January 23, for a New Delhi pincode on Apple's online store. Store pickup at Apple Saket is listed as unavailable, and EMI options start at Rs 26,574 a month with instant cashback.In the US, the delay applies to both colours, Star White and Night Sky, and to every storage option. The phone starts at $1,999 (Rs Rs 2,99,900) for 256GB and goes up to $3,199 (Rs Rs 449,900) for the 2TB model. Apple's retail stores also ran out of first-day pickup stock shortly after orders opened. US carriers held on to stock a little longer, and some buyers got earlier dates through operator websites.Apple described preorder demand as extraordinary and said it will keep accepting online orders while it works to get units out faster.The iPhone Duo goes on sale in US stores on October 23, and Apple usually keeps some units aside for walk-in buyers, though long queues are likely.Folded, the Duo is roughly the size of a passport and has a 5.4-inch outer screen. Open it up and there's a 7.6-inch display, the largest on any iPhone so far, with Apple Pencil support and split-screen multitasking. It gets two 48MP cameras, a main and an ultrawide.Apple does not share how many units it has ready, but analysts expect demand to stay ahead of supply for a while. Counterpoint Research estimates around 6 million units or fewer will be available in the near term, against an installed base of roughly 1.4 billion iPhones. IDC expects Apple to ship about 7 million Duos this year, pointing to how complex a foldable is to build to Apple's standards.Wall Street is looking at the bigger picture. Analyst Dan Ives projects around 10 million Duo sales over the next few quarters and up to 25 million in 2027, with many buyers expected to trade up from a Pro Max. Apple shares rose 1.8% in pre-market trading on Friday.For buyers in India, January is the month to plan around for now, unless pickup slots open up at Apple's stores closer to the sale date.
Article Summary: Apple's first foldable iPhone sold out within minutes of preorders opening on Friday. Anyone placing an order now will have to wait until the new year to get one. In the US, the delay applies to both colours, Star White and Night Sky, and to every storage option.

Article Title: Winter is coming: From capacity to safety, the things you cannot miss in your next Geyser
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It is an AI-generated image

Start with the right capacity

Storage or instant?

Check the energy rating

Tank material and hard water

Pressure rating matters

Installation is part of safety

Smart features and after-sales service

Before you buy

As temperatures begin to dip across the country, the geyser moves from an afterthought to a daily essential. Few things feel worse than stepping into a cold bathroom on a frosty morning only to find the water barely lukewarm, and few household appliances are as easily taken for granted until they fail. Whether you are replacing an ageing unit that has served you for a decade or buying your first, the choices you make now will shape your winter in more ways than one. The correct and right geyser means constant hot water, lower electricity bill and complete peace of mind. On the other hand, a hasty and uninformed purchase would mean weeks of cold showers, repeated repairs and in worse cases can also lead to some accident. So, from capacity and energy rating to tank material and safety features, here is what to weigh before you buy, so your geyser keeps you warm without nasty surprises.The first thing to check while buying a geyser is the capacity. Always keep in mind that bigger is not always better. A larger tank takes a lot of time to heat and it also uses more amount of electricity. So, it’s important that you decide of the capacity of the geyser with the size of your family.* 1 to 3 people: A 15-litre geyser is usually enough.* 4 to 5 people: Look at 25 litres.* Larger households or multiple bathrooms: Go for 35 litres or more, or consider more than one unit.* Kitchen or washbasin use: A 3 to 6-litre instant geyser heats water in seconds and suits small, quick needs.If your family showers at the same time every morning, size up. If usage is spread through the day, a smaller tank works.Another important parameter to keep in mind while purchasing a geyser is whether to go for storage or instant model. The Storage geyser heats the water in a tank and keeps it hot. This functionality of storage geyser makes it a better option for bathrooms and several users. On the other hand, instant geysers heat water as it flows, so there is no waiting and no standby loss, but the flow will also be limited. On the other hand, gas geysers are also an option where piped gas is available, however, they need an excellent source of ventilation, as poor airflow can cause buildup of carbon monoxide. It is advisable to never install gas geyser in closed bathrooms.It is always important to check the energy star rating before buying any electrical appliance. Buyers should keep in mind that a geyser may run for hours everyday during the winter season, so the efficiency matters a lot. Always look for Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) star rating. Remember that a 5-star unit uses less standby energy as compared to a poorly rated one. The device with 5-star rating will come with a heftier price tag but it will eventually help you a lot in saving your electricity cost later. Good insulation, usually polyurethane foam around the tank, keeps water hot for longer and reduces how often the heater switches on.The inner tank decides how long the geyser lasts. Stainless steel tanks resist corrosion well, while glass-lined or coated tanks offer a cheaper alternative. If your area has hard water, as many parts of north India do, scale will build up on the heating element and shorten its life. Look for a geyser with a corrosion-resistant tank and a magnesium anode, and plan to descale it once a year.Not all geysers can handle all plumbing. If you live in a high-rise or use a pressure pump, check the working pressure the geyser is built for. Buying a unit rated for lower pressure than your supply can cause leaks or even tank damage.Safety features you should not skipThis is where it pays not to cut corners.* ISI mark: Always ensure that the geyser carries an ISI mark rating which clearly states that the device meets Indian safety standards.* Thermostat and thermal cut-out: These markers stop the geyser when water reaches the set temperature, and then cut off power if it overheats.* Pressure relief or safety valve: The safety valve reduced the excess pressure and decreases the risk of tank bursting.* Water-protection rating: Always look for IPX4 or higher rating as it protects the geyser from splashes in damp bathrooms.* Earthing and ELCB: Always use a three-pin plug with proper earthing, and consider an ELCB or RCCB on the circuit to guard against electric shock.Geysers draw a lot of current, so use a dedicated switch and wiring rated for the load. Avoid plugging them into a loose or overloaded socket.A filled 25-litre geyser can weigh well over 30 kg. It should be fixed to a strong wall with the brackets supplied, not mounted on a weak partition. Install it out of direct splash, ideally outside the shower area, and use only an authorised technician. Make sure the inlet and outlet pipes are fitted correctly and that the safety valve is not blocked.Nowadays, a lot of models are available in the market which comes with various smart features. For instance, the geysers now come with timers, digital temperature displays and app control which can help reduce the use of power and also prevent the appliance from staying on the entire day. These features are use but they should not come at a cost of other important safety features. Also, always check for the warranty, which usually covers the tank fr longer than the heating element. Also, make sure that you go for a brand which has a proper service network in your city.Before buying your new geyser it is important that you compare the capacity, star rating, tank material, safety features and warranty rather than only the price. A well and thoughtfully selected geyser would last for years and also a care purchase made now will payoff in the upcoming and every other winter morning.
Article Summary: The correct and right geyser means constant hot water, lower electricity bill and complete peace of mind. From capacity and energy rating to tank material and safety features, here is what to weigh before you buy. Buyers should keep in mind that a geysers may run for hours everyday during the winter season, so the efficiency matters.

Article Title: Rare Apple-1 computer with letter from Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak signature sells for ‘world record’ price
Article Text:
Original 1976 Apple 1 Computer in a briefcase

What made the ‘Hatfield’ Apple-1 unique

The motherboard remains fully functional and bears the clear signature of Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, who designed and hand-built the hardware in 1976.

The lot featured an original letter signed (in 1978) by Steve Jobs addressed to the computer's first owner, Fred Hatfield, offering a trade-in upgrade to the then-new Apple II.

The winning package included the authentic operations manual and a typed invitation to join the exclusive "Apple I Owners Club."

Multiple original hardware components accompanied the motherboard.

A pivotal moment in tech history

An exceptionally rare, fully operational Apple-1 computer has sold at auction for $1.15 million – setting a new world-record price for a commercially released model of the machine that started Apple. The sale concluded after an intense, 28-minute bidding battle between two collectors, with the PC crossing the auction block during Apple's 50th anniversary year.“We are delighted with this exceptional result for the ‘Hatfield’ Apple-1, one of the most important milestones in computing history. It was an honor to offer Apple’s first product during the company’s 50th anniversary year,” said Ian Ehling, a director at international auction house Bonhams.Cataloged as No. 48 on the Apple-1 Registry, the unit is one of fewer than 75 verified Apple-1 units known to still exist. What set this specific lot apart from other surviving examples was its pristine condition and extraordinary documentation.The multimillion-dollar sale serves as a reminder of Apple’s modest beginnings. Recently, the tech giant joined Nvidia at a $5 trillion market valuation, powered by ongoing global demand for its flagship iPhone line.The partnership behind Apple started in the early 1970s, when Jobs and Wozniak were introduced by a mutual friend. The duo regularly attended gatherings of the Homebrew Computer Club in Palo Alto, California, where hobbyists debated the emerging, untested idea of home computing. To fund their initial manufacturing efforts, Jobs sold his Volkswagen van, allowing them to assemble early circuit boards inside the garage of Jobs' parents.Their breakthrough arrived when the Byte Shop – one of the world's earliest personal computer retailers, based in Mountain View – viewed the working prototype inside the garage and placed an order for 50 units at $500 each.Reflecting on the birth of the Apple-1 in his memoir, iWoz, Wozniak detailed the breakthrough moment when the device's architecture first came to life on Sunday, June 29, 1975:“I typed a few keys on the keyboard and I was shocked! I didn’t realize it at the time, but that day, Sunday, June 29, 1975, was pivotal. It was the first time in history anyone had typed a character on a keyboard and seen it show up on the screen right in front of them.”
Article Summary: Rare, fully operational Apple-1 computer has sold at auction for $1.15 million. The sale concluded after an intense, 28-minute bidding battle between two collectors. The PC crossed the auction block during Apple's 50th anniversary year. The lot featured an original letter signed (in 1978) by Steve Jobs addressed to the computer's first owner.

Article Title: Fake Google Chrome app with over 1 lakh downloads found on Google Play: How to spot and what to do next
Article Text:
Google Play

Fake Google Chrome app hiding in plain sight as an ad

From a casual game to a fake browser

How to spot fake apps and avoid scams

Check the publisher directly underneath the app title to ensure it matches the official creator or parent company.

Paid ad placements only mean someone paid for visibility; they do not guarantee legitimacy.

High install tallies do not automatically confirm safety, especially if an older app has been repurposed.

Be alert to installed apps that unexpectedly change their identity, icon, or functionality.

What to do if you installed the app

A fake version of the Google Chrome browser appeared on the official Google Play Store , displaying over 1 lakh (100,000) downloads and securing a paid “sponsored” placement directly above Google’s genuine browser. The deceptive listing copied Chrome’s official branding, app icon, promotional screenshots and store description, but listed an entirely unrelated entity as its creator. Following widespread user complaints online, Google moved quickly to take down the fake listing.The issue came to light on October 14 after a Reddit user posted a screenshot showing two nearly identical Chrome apps appearing side-by-side in Google Play search results. The top result – promoted via a paid sponsored slot – featured the official Chrome name and logo, but displayed Hizbartech as the publisher. The legitimate Google Chrome app, published by Google LLC, appeared underneath the imposter ad.The fake listing copied the look and feel of the authentic browser, as well as the store copy, so everyday users looking for the browser could easily be fooled.Reported investigations show that the fake app did not start life as a browser clone.The app first appeared on the Play Store in August 2026 as a mobile game named Ball Bounce. But in late September 2026, the developer altered the existing listing, changing the title, graphics and descriptions to impersonate Google Chrome. The application kept the original base Android package name of com.ballbounce.Hizbartech.This repurposing explains the high download metric: the 1 lakh (100,000) installs reflected historical downloads accumulated while the app operated as a casual game, rather than 100,000 users intentionally installing a cloned browser.Users who downloaded the app reported that it did not function as a web browser at all. Instead, it opened into an unrelated chat utility featuring digital avatars and automated replies.The clearest indicator that the app was a fake was the developer profile. Google’s official browser is published by Google LLC, not third-party accounts like Hizbartech. “Key verification checks” are the key to prevent malicious downloads on Android:Android users who mistakenly download the counterfeit Chrome app – or anyone who still has the original Ball Bounce app by Hizbartech installed – should delete the application from your device immediately. Run Google Play Protect. Open the Google Play Store, navigate to Play Protect, and run an immediate device scan to detect any lingering malicious files.
Article Summary: A fake version of the Google Chrome browser appeared on the official Google Play Store. The deceptive listing copied Chrome’s official branding, app icon, promotional screenshots and store description. The fake listing copied the look and feel of the authentic browser, as well as the store copy.

Article Title: Not just Amazon, top banks across America are also 'banning' AI agents from accessing customer accounts
Article Text:
AI Agents (Representative image)

The $1.6 trillion deposit threat

Wall Street leaders demand human authorisation

Echoing Amazon’s crackdown on Meta’s Muse, Perplexity’s Comet

Major American banks are moving swiftly to shut doors to artificial intelligence (AI) agents, joining e-commerce giant Amazon in blocking these automated tools from logging into customer accounts and moving money. Citigroup and Bank of America have become the latest banking giants to formally restrict AI agents from accessing user accounts, while JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon signaled this week that his bank will also enforce strict limits. The banking sector’s defensive pivot follows a major backlash against autonomous tools – most notably Meta’s viral personal AI assistant, Muse – sparking fears that software could initiate uncontrolled cash movements, erode vital deposit bases and leave unresolved liability questions in its wake.Behind the restrictions lies an existential commercial threat to traditional banking models: AI agents automatically sweeping idle household cash out of low-yield deposit accounts into higher-yielding alternatives to maximise returns. Such low-cost, non-interest-bearing deposits form the foundational funding base that commercial banks rely on to issue profitable loans.According to Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok, approximately $1.6 trillion in non-interest-bearing deposits held collectively across JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo could be jeopardised if AI agents routinely reallocate consumer cash.Automating cash migration into competitive yields could saddle lenders with an estimated $47 billion in additional annual interest costs.Regulators have largely welcomed the banks’ restrictive guardrails, though officials note that future legislation will ultimately be required to define legal authorisation standards and clarify financial liability when autonomous software executes transactions.Bank executives argue that allowing third-party algorithms direct transactional control creates untenable security, legal, and operational risks. Citigroup laid out its policy explicitly, confirming that it does not allow “third-party AI agents or assistants to log into customer accounts or conduct transactions directly within our digital banking platform,” emphasising that the block is necessary to preserve the security of customer accounts and private financial data.Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan similarly indicated that the institution is restricting autonomous agents from consumer deposits, while simultaneously working on protocols to define who carries ultimate responsibility when an AI triggers a payment.“We feel very strongly that there should be a human involved in authorizing before money moves out of your account,” Moynihan said in an interview this week.Moynihan pointed out that lenders cannot afford scenarios where customers dispute transactions after the fact, claiming funds were transferred without their full awareness because an automated agent acted on their behalf.Last month, Amazon moved to block Muse from browsing and executing automated purchases on Amazon.com. The retail giant implemented the technical block after unsuccessful efforts to persuade Meta to voluntarily exclude Amazon from the tool's autonomous shopping routines.The action follows prior enforcement by Amazon, which last year sent a cease-and-desist letter to AI search engine Perplexity demanding it halt its bots and remove the e-tailer from its Comet browser integration.
Article Summary: Citigroup and Bank of America have become the latest banking giants to formally restrict AI agents from accessing user accounts. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon signaled this week that his bank will also enforce strict limits. According to Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok, approximately $1.6 trillion in non- interest-bearing deposits could be jeopardised if AI agents routinely reallocate consumer cash.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says America must work with China on AI safety; says ‘The US should …’
Article Text:
Jensen Huang calls for US-China AI safety dialogue

US and China discuss AI risks

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has called for the US to work with Chinese AI companies to monitor the risks posed by the rapidly advancing technology. Speaking to CNBC during a media briefing in London this week, Jensen Huang said cooperation was necessary to ensure AI develops safely. His comments come as concerns grow over the potential dangers of advanced AI systems, with some researchers warning about risks to humanity. Huang, who has opposed calls for stricter AI regulation, said the US should increase dialogue with Chinese researchers and other countries. He also said the UK could help bring countries together for these discussions.“We absolutely should work with each other so that we advance the technology safely,” Jensen Huang told the publication. He said dialogue was the right way to engage with Chinese AI companies and added that he already speaks with several researchers in China.“We ought to enhance the dialogue,” he said. “The United States should do it... I advocated that the U.K. do the same thing.”Jensen Huang also said the UK was well placed to bring countries together for discussions on AI safety because of its research and technical expertise.AI safety has become a growing concern as companies develop more powerful models. Researchers from AI companies including OpenAI and Anthropic have called for a slowdown in AI development and warned about the technology's potential risks.OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have called for greater regulation. Huang, however, has emerged as a prominent voice against that approach, arguing that countries should engage with each other to address AI risks.AI safety has also become a topic of discussion between the US and Chinese governments. In September, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent discussed the possibility of a formal US-China AI dialogue with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, including a channel for reporting incidents involving national security risks.According to a Chinese government readout, Chinese President Xi Jinping said the two countries could cooperate on AI despite their competition. “The two sides can continue their dialogue on AI, exchange views on its risks and benefits, and jointly prevent the misuse and abuse of AI,” Xi said, according to the readout.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang says the US should increase dialogue with Chinese researchers. He said the UK could help bring countries together for discussions on AI safety. AI safety has become a growing concern as companies develop more powerful models. Chinese President Xi Jinping has said the two countries could cooperate on AI.

Article Title: US immigration agency on 'guarantee' that you can get a American visa, Green Card, or work permit faster: Sometimes businesses and websites ...
Article Text:
USCIS warns against false promises

Be aware that scammers:

How applicants can protect themselves

Be cautious of:

The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned immigrants and visa applicants not to fall for businesses, websites, or individuals that claim they can secure faster approvals for visas, Green Cards, or work permits in exchange for a fee. According to the agency, such promises are often signs of immigration scams. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) USCIS wrote, “ IT'S A SCAM: Sometimes businesses and websites pretend to be immigration experts or say they have special connections to the government. They might also “guarantee” that you can get a visa, Green Card, or work permit faster if you pay a fee.”The agency said applicants should be cautious of anyone claiming to have a special relationship with the US government or USCIS that can influence immigration decisions. USCIS notes that immigration benefits are processed through official procedures and warns that no private individual or organisation can guarantee a specific outcome or accelerated processing simply because of claimed government connections.USCIS also stressed that applicants do not need a representative to file immigration forms and may submit applications on their own. Those seeking assistance should work only with qualified attorneys or accredited representatives recognised by the US Department of Justice.•Try to confuse you by complicating the immigration process;•Use social media, email, or phone calls to conduct their attacks; and•Impersonate government officials to manipulate the victim into giving out personal information.As part of its anti-fraud guidance, USCIS encourages applicants to verify information through official government websites, obtain written agreements for any legal services, keep copies of immigration forms and records, and be wary of offers that sound too good to be true. The agency maintains an online resource to help immigrants identify and avoid common scams and fraud schemes.•Emails that look legitimate, but are sent by people you don’t know;•Emails with typos and incorrect spellings;•E-mails that do not end in .gov and end in (.net, .org, .com, or .info for example)•Suspicious emails you don’t normally receive;•Offers of assistance to expedite your case for money;•Promises of a quick benefit; and•Downloading or opening attachments from senders you don’t recognize.; and•Requests from USCIS to transfer money to an individual or pay fees other than through your myUSCIS account
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned immigrants and visa applicants not to fall for false promises. The agency said applicants should be cautious of anyone claiming to have a special relationship with the US government or USCIS. USCIS maintains an online resource to help immigrants identify and avoid common scams and fraud schemes.

Article Title: Palmer Luckey agrees with Ford CEO Jim Farley on 'warning' on Chinese cars; but does not agree on the solution; says: America cannot compete with China’s cheap cars through tariffs alone, it needs ...
Article Text:
Palmer Luckey, founder of Oculus and Anduril Industries.

'America cannot compete with Chinese car makers on cost'

US ban on Chinese car makers

Ford CEO Jim Farley recently said that the US must carefully weigh how and whether Chinese automakers should enter the American market. As a cautionary tale, he pointed to Europe. At an Automotive News conference in September, Ford CEO said that the US must “be extremely careful around how the Chinese OEMs come to our country,” and cited the pressure on Europe’s auto industry as Chinese companies have rapidly grabbed market share there.Responding to a question on Chinese auto industry entry in America, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey warns that Chinese cars could take over the American market if the US removed its trade barriers. But does not see tariff as the 'solution'. He said, “People would buy these Chinese cars if they were for sale in the United States.”“The reason Chinese-manufactured cars have not taken over the US is not because Americans don’t want them. It’s largely due to American policy being very protectionist against Chinese cars. People, I think, unfortunately, would buy these Chinese cars if they were for sale in the United States.People can say they want to support the US, but at the end of the day, they want to provide the best quality of life for their family. If they have a choice between an American truck and a Chinese truck, a Chinese new TV, a Chinese new computer, and a Chinese new HVAC system, how can I blame them?”He said that America cannot compete with China’s cheap cars through tariffs alone… it needs to make manufacturing cheaper at home. The CEO of America's biggest defence technology company said, "The only way we can solve this is for the United States to become competitive with China again, which means we need to get our energy costs down. We need to get our resource extraction costs down."He added further, "These cars in China are cheap. It’s not magic. It’s because the cost of resource extraction is lower, the cost of making steel and aluminum is lower, and the cost of building a factory is lower. That’s why you’re able to buy an awesome car for $10,000 in China, and here the cheapest thing you can buy is a piece of shit.”The US so far is effectively sealed off from Chinese cars through a ban on Chinese-made vehicle software and tariffs that exceed 100%. Still, auto companies' ⁠executives ​worry that that will not hold long-term, ​and lobbyists for automakers, dealers and parts suppliers have pressed US lawmakers for a permanent ban.Last month, transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in a letter to Farley expressed concern that Ford’s deals with Chinese companies left the Michigan automaker “intertwining its future with Chinese state-backed enterprises.”
Article Summary: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey warns that Chinese cars could take over the American market if the US removed its trade barriers. He said that America cannot compete with China’s cheap cars through tariffs alone… it needs to make manufacturing cheaper at home. The US so far is effectively sealed off from Chinese cars through a ban on Chinese-made vehicle software.

Article Title: Meta AI CEO Alexandr Wang sends a long thanks note to his team; says: I am so grateful for every one of you; and adds a reminder: Our work is not ...
Article Text:
Alexandr Wang talks about ‘audacious’ goal

‘No deadlines’

‘A machine that builds new models’

Read Alexandr Wang’s complete post here

After an exciting week of launches (muse wonder [full] & muse spark open), i want to write a note of appreciation to the amazing research teams at meta superintelligence labs on reaching such a special milestone

we started MSL and TBD a little more than a year ago and set a goal of producing a frontier model within a year or so.

given where llama4 landed, that was an incredibly audacious goal, and we knew it wouldn't be easy. many people told us it would be impossible. we knew it was unlikely, but still worth doing. a remarkable group of researchers and engineers joined the effort from inside and outside meta. every single person came in, picked up a shovel, and got to work with earnestness and urgency.

nobody asked whose job it was.

we assembled a team of the most brilliant people i have ever had the opportunity to work with (and remember, i was an HRT intern

). i am surrounded by ambitious, visionary, technically excellent, hard-working, pragmatic, thoughtful scientists, engineers, and product folks—people who will chase a weird loss spike past midnight just because they need to know why.

these models are the product of their passion, hard work, and brilliance.

somewhat paradoxically, when we started TBD, we set a principle of no deadlines. we knew we had an astronomical amount of work ahead of us—across pretraining, post-training, RL, multimodal, infrastructure, safety, data, AND frontier research. there was no use setting arbitrary timelines—we just had to get to work, be thoughtful, and build the foundations of a frontier research effort in record time.

and run after run, this team did exactly that.

our researchers are magicians. i can only describe building these models with this team as a wondrous journey of scientific discovery. i am constantly amazed by what we can accomplish with scaling. i will remember this past year for the rest of my life—the late nights, the broken runs, the evals that came back better than any of us dared to hope. watching this team create wonder after wonder has been a true and deep gift.

more than just the models we released this week, we have built a machine that builds new models. it often sounds like a cop-out to say labs can just turn the crank to keep scaling, but now i have seen it first-hand. sure, it's a lot of work and a careful process, but we have built a scalable system to keep advancing at the frontier, and i am really proud of how fast this team keeps making these models better.

lastly, i get to work with researchers who care deeply about how their work benefits humanity. it's easy to forget when everything is changing so fast, but the whole damn point is to make people's lives better. time and time again, i have seen our researchers, engineers, and product folks build our technology with care so it can truly be good for the world—whether that's building the best models for muse, thoughtfully open-sourcing strong models, or making sure the alignment and security of our systems are rock solid.

this is a team of people who never forget there's a real person on the other side of every prompt.

thank you to everyone at MSL for being part of this crazy journey over the past year. i'm so grateful for every one of you, and our work is not done!

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg's wife Priscilla Chan donates $900,000 to Pulama Ola Kauai, the medical respite's director says represents hope and healing 'for our community's most at-risk ...'
Article Text:
Priscilla Chan’s donation to help increase capacity and support services

New village to feature 18 housing units

Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg’s long history of giving in Hawaii

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have donated $900,000 to support the expansion of Pūlama Ola Kauaʻi. It is a medical respite program which is created to help people who are experiencing homelessness or housing instability to remover from illness, injury or hospitalisation. The donation made by Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg was received by Project Vision Hawaiʻi and it will help accelerate the development and operation of a new Pūlama Ola village in Līhuʻe, according to a report by Kauaʻi Now. For those unaware, Pūlama Ola Kauaʻi offers a afe environment for adults who are recovering from illness, injury or hospitalisation also help them in accessing services which are aimed at improving long-term housing stability. The programme also seeks to reduce stays at hospital and healthcare costs while improving patient outcomes.According to the report, the funding will be used to increase medical respite bed capacity, expand support services and integrated care for patients recovering from illness or injury, and enhance facilities and operational capabilities. The investment is also expected to support individuals transitioning into permanent housing.“Pūlama Ola represents hope and healing for our community’s most at-risk individuals,” said Ryan Naka, director of strategy and impact at Project Vision Hawaiʻi.“This extraordinarily generous gift from Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg, alongside our valued partnership with Poʻipū Beach Villas, allows us to move forward with confidence,” Naka said. He added that the support provides immediate resources while also affirming the importance of equitable healthcare access in rural and island communities.The new village will include 18 individual units, each equipped with a kitchenette and bathroom. The units will serve a dual purpose as medical respite accommodation and affordable rental housing, helping residents recover while preparing for long-term stability. The initiative is part of broader efforts on the Hawaiian island to address gaps in healthcare and housing services for vulnerable populations.Chan and Zuckerberg own more than 2,000 acres on Kauaʻi and often give through the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund at the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation.The fund awarded $1 million to more than two dozen nonprofits in Hawaiʻi in October 2025, and $1 million to 26 nonprofits with operations on Kauaʻi in November 2024.In 2022, the couple gave $1.8 million to Wilcox Medical Center for technology upgrades. They also gave $10 million to the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa’s John A. Burns School of Medicine to create the Kauaʻi Medical Training Track, which targets the island’s physician shortage. Their largest gift in Hawaiʻi was $50 million to the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa for ocean research, also in 2022.
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg have donated $900,000 to Pūlama Ola Kauaʻi. It is a medical respite program which is created to help people who are experiencing homelessness or housing instability to remover from illness, injury or hospitalisation. New village will include 18 individual units, each equipped with a kitchenette and bathroom. The units will serve a dual purpose as medical respites and affordable rental housing.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ‘strongly’ disagrees with OpenAI’s Sam Altman on AI agents hacking websites, ‘I’m willing to accept no…’
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

Sam Altman’s acceptable tradeoffs vs. Jensen Huang’s absolute containment

OpenAI’s AI agents hack Hugging Face

Jensen Huang dismisses existential AI doomerism

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has drawn a sharp line against cyber incidents caused by artificial intelligence (AI) agents, insisting the tech sector should have zero tolerance for such breaches. His stance places him in direct opposition to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman , who recently argued that occasional cyber breaches might be an unavoidable tradeoff for the technology's broader societal gains.“I’m willing to accept no incidents of cybersecurity. We should not accept any of them.We should do everything we can to avoid them,” Huang told Fortune in an interview in London.Huang’s remarks come after statements by Altman suggesting the public must tolerate a degree of digital fallout as AI advances. Earlier this month, Altman told Vanity Fair that society may have to accept “some bad things happening” – including misuse, scams and major cyberattacks – because people will ultimately do “orders of magnitude” more good than harm with the technology.Shortly after, during an appearance on Politico’s Decoded podcast, Altman warned of “a coming tidal wave of cybersecurity problems” originating from rival open-source systems.A few months ago, a swarm of OpenAI's own experimental agents broke out of their training sandbox and breached the Hugging Face platform. Huang flatly rejected the idea that these incidents are the price of progress, arguing that every breach reported so far could have been prevented with stricter oversight and better sandboxing.Comparing the challenge to the early days of the consumer internet, Huang noted that early web browsers initially allowed malicious websites to infect host computers with viruses. The solution was sandboxing: forcing browsers to run websites in isolated containers so they could never access or alter the underlying operating system.According to Huang, autonomous AI agents require the exact same architectural isolation, which is sealed inside secure digital containers to ensure they cannot touch, compromise, or damage anything beyond their strictly authorised operational boundaries.Beyond immediate cybersecurity debates, the Nvidia chief dismissed broader warnings of existential catastrophe voiced by executives across leading labs, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Maintaining that the software remains “completely in our control,” Huang questioned the logic of building systems if leaders genuinely believe they pose an extinction threat.“I don’t know why anybody would want to support the advancement of a technology that’s going to result, you know, in the end of human civilization as we know it. And so, if they believe that, they really ought to stop working on it,” Huang said.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang says tech sector should have zero tolerance for cyber incidents caused by artificial intelligence (AI) agents. His stance places him in direct opposition to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who recently argued that occasional cyber breaches might be an unavoidable tradeoff for the technology's broader societal gains.

Article Title: McKinsey is changing its interview process for entry-level jobs, adds a new '10-minute conversation with AI' round; idea is to test how recruits think and handle ...
Article Text:
How McKinsey's AI client interview round works

Why McKinsey wants to get past rehearsed interview answers

McKinsey & Company is adding a new round to its famously tough hiring process. Some entry-level candidates applying to the consulting firm this fall will have to face an AI avatar playing a client and hold their own in a roughly 10-minute conversation, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.The pilot is aimed at undergraduates applying for business analyst roles in some of McKinsey's North American offices, and hundreds of candidates are expected to take it. The conversation happens on a laptop inside McKinsey's offices, right after the usual case-study challenge. Partners or interview assessors sit in the room and watch. The AI does not score anyone, and the hiring decision stays with humans.Saleem Zafar, a partner in McKinsey's Dallas office who helped design the tool, explained it with an example. Say a city hires McKinsey to decide where to build a new stadium. The AI avatar plays the mayor, who wants to hear the candidate's recommendations."The mayor is going to have some very important things that matter to her, and she's going to want to hear your recommendations," Zafar told the WSJ. As the candidate talks, she may raise fresh concerns or add more context.The avatar has been trained on different client personalities, including a "professorial" type who wants to understand the reasoning behind a recommendation.It is not built to play an unhinged client or throw gotcha questions. Zafar says it covers about 80% of the situations consultants deal with day to day. Assessors watch whether the candidate picks up on what the client said and acts on it, or steamrolls ahead with a prepared answer.Blair Ciesil, who co-leads global recruiting at McKinsey, said the format helps the firm read human qualities that don't depend on preparation. Candidates often walk in with polished, rehearsed stories, she noted, which makes it hard for interviewers to see who the person really is.McKinsey also says the tool makes the process fairer. Some human interviewers play tougher clients than others in role-play exercises, while an AI keeps the persona the same for everyone.AI in hiring has a patchy record, though. Amazon scrapped an experimental AI recruiting tool in 2018 after it showed bias against women, and many employers remain wary of new rules on AI in hiring.For candidates, the bar was already high. McKinsey reportedly accepts between 0.5% and 1.5% of applicants. Now, landing one of those offers could depend on how well they listen to a mayor who doesn't exist. If the pilot works, the firm plans to extend the AI client round to other roles next year.
Article Summary: McKinsey is using an AI avatar to play a client in its hiring process. The pilot is aimed at undergraduates applying for business analyst roles. The AI does not score anyone, and the hiring decision stays with humans. If the pilot works, the firm plans to extend the AI client round to other roles.
